    Georian Humans¶

    Humans are the most populous and geographically dispersed sapient species on Ge'or. All Georian humans descend from the survivors of the Glorious Alliance crash approximately 15,000 years before the Great Divergence. After generations on a world with 1.37× Old Earth's gravity, Georian humans developed denser bone structure, slightly more compact frames, and greater baseline physical endurance than their Earth ancestors — adaptations now invisible to them but measurable against historical records in the Archive of the Traveler.

    Biology¶

    Georian humans are shorter on average than Old Earth humans (men ~165cm, women ~155cm) due to the higher gravity compressing spinal development over generations. Mage-cell expression varies widely: some bloodlines produce powerful mages, others none at all. Dilution through interbreeding with non-magical populations has gradually reduced the number of pure mage-blood families.

    Lifespan averages 70-80 years without magical intervention. Healing mages in populated areas make disease and injury far less lethal than medieval Earth equivalents. Lost-spell healers capable of regenerating limbs exist but are vanishingly rare.

    Distribution¶

    Humans can be found on every continent except Lung and Sister, where the Machine and Hive civilizations maintain no organic populations. The highest concentrations are on Erisdar, the Demon Continent, and Merratodoni.

    Major human sub-races include the Axels of North Erisdar (tall, blond, Norse-coded), the Baothians of Central Erisdar (Germanic-coded, descendants of Baoth's citizenry), the Mago of East Erisdar (Slavic-coded), the Irikod of South Erisdar (Mediterranean-coded), and the Makod of Dissenbarg (Ancient Greek-coded). All are fully inter-fertile — distinctions are cultural and physical, not species-level.

    Society¶

    Human societies span the full spectrum of governance from theocratic empire (Erisian Empire) to plutocratic trade republic (Anos Plutocracy) to feudal duchy (Archduchy of the Kennberg). No single human culture dominates; their adaptability is their defining trait.

    Relations with Other Races¶

    Dwarves: Generally cordial. Dwarves value craftsmanship and humans value trade — the relationship is pragmatic and stable. Mixed communities exist in Dwarvengor and the mountain cities of East Erisdar.

    Elves: Complex. Elves view humans as short-lived and impulsive; humans view elves as aloof and slow to act. The Fallen Elves of the Mystical Forest (Central Erisdar) share more cultural affinity with humans than with their Erisdarian kin, having rejected elven isolationism after the Demonic War.

    Beast Races: Variable. Trading relationships in West Erisdar cities like Augamouth and Astravayne are cooperative. Rural tensions exist where territorial claims overlap. The beastmen-heavy multiracial cities of the west represent the most integrated human-beast societies on the continent.

    Demons: Historically tense due to Erisian Church crusades against the Demon Continent, but individual demon-human relationships exist in trade ports like Demon's Horn. The Church's propaganda paints demons as inherently evil; the reality is far more nuanced.

    Orcs: Strained by cultural prejudice. Orcs face systemic discrimination despite being a civilized species with their own kingdom. Human merchants in Augamouth have learned to work with orcish traders; human peasants in border regions still tell monster stories.
